data.title: OCI Announces EGM Approval and Updated Indicative Timetable for Orascom Construction Combination
data.description:
AMSTERDAM, Oct. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- OCI N.V. ("OCI" or the "Company") (Euronext: OCI) today announced that its shareholders have approved all resolutions relating to the proposed business combination between OCI and Orascom Construction PLC ("Orascom Construction") (the "Combination"). OCI also provides shareholders with an updated indicative timetable for the Combination, including the expected delisting date for OCI Shares from Euronext Amsterdam.

Shareholder Information and Key Dates

  • Today, the Extraordinary General Meeting approved all resolutions put to a vote, including the resolutions relating to the Combination and the OCIN Sale. Each resolution was also supported by a majority of votes cast by minority shareholders. The detailed voting results are available on OCI's website in accordance with applicable requirements.
  • Euronext Amsterdam has approved the delisting of the OCI Shares effective as of 27 November 2026, resulting in the final day OCI Shares can be traded on Euronext Amsterdam being 26 November 2026, subject to receipt of the required regulatory approvals in the relevant jurisdictions, and any other developments that may affect the delisting date. The ex-date for the Distribution of OC Shares to OCI shareholders is expected to be 27 November 2026.
  • The Tender Closing Date under NNS's voluntary offer (the "Offer") is 17 November 2026 at 17:40 CET. Shareholders wishing to tender their OCI Shares should contact their bank, broker or other intermediary sufficiently in advance, as intermediaries may apply earlier instruction deadlines. Further updates regarding the Offer, including on the expected timetable of relevant events relating to the Offer, are expected to be made by NNS with due observance of applicable rules and regulations.
  • Subject to completion of the required corporate, regulatory, listing and settlement steps, and subject to further announcements by NNS on the timetable for the Offer, OCI currently expects the crediting of Orascom Construction shares ("OC Shares") to eligible shareholder accounts to commence on or around 8 December 2026. The date on which an individual shareholder receives OC Shares may differ, potentially significantly, depending on the shareholder's circumstances, the completeness of settlement information provided, and the processes of the relevant intermediary.
  • The timetable for the Combination continues to be indicative. OCI will keep its shareholders informed as further information becomes available, including but not limited to as information on the Offer is made public by NNS in accordance with the relevant statutory notice requirements.

Indicative Timetable

The table below sets out certain expected key dates and times in connection with the Combination. Except where otherwise indicated, all dates and times are indicative only, reflect the Company's current expectations and remain subject to change. Capitalised terms not otherwise defined in this press release have the meanings given to them in the EGM Circular or, as applicable, NNS's Offer Memorandum.

Additional Information Regarding the Distribution

Subject to completion of the Combination, the OC Shares will be distributed to eligible OCI shareholders in accordance with the transaction structure described in the EGM Circular. Shareholders who are eligible to receive OC Shares but whose complete or validated settlement information has not been provided (by them or, as applicable, their bank or broker) by the relevant operational deadlines may not receive their OC Shares at the same time as other shareholders. Their entitlements will instead be handled in accordance with the applicable suspense arrangements described in the EGM materials.

OCI encourages shareholders to read the 'Shareholder Decision Guide' and the other information regarding the Combination available on OCI's website. The Shareholder Decision Guide advises shareholders wishing to receive OC Shares to contact their bank, broker or custodian as soon as possible to confirm whether, and subject to what conditions, that intermediary supports the Distribution. The indicative timetable  assumes that OCI Shares validly tendered during the Offer Period or Post-Closing Acceptance Period will settle under the Offer before the record date for the Distribution. If the Offer timetable is longer than currently assumed, including if NNS determines that the Post-Closing Acceptance Period will continue for two weeks, the timetable for implementation of the Combination will be adjusted accordingly.

Additional Information Regarding Dutch Dividend Withholding Tax

As described in the EGM Circular, OCI will sell a number of OC Shares corresponding to the percentage of the total value of the Distribution to be withheld on account of Dutch dividend withholding tax. Because the number of OC Shares to be sold will be determined by reference to the applicable withholding percentage, the number of OC Shares distributed to shareholders will not depend on whether the proceeds of the sale are sufficient to cover the Dutch dividend withholding tax payable.

Completion of the sale of such OC Shares will not be a condition precedent to OCI making the Distribution and is not expected to delay or otherwise affect the timing of the Distribution to shareholders.

If the proceeds of such sale are insufficient to cover the Dutch dividend withholding tax payable in connection with the Distribution, the shortfall will be funded for the account of the combined company. No additional OC Shares will be withheld from relevant shareholders solely as a result of such shortfall.

Important Notice Regarding Timing

If any of the dates and/or times set out in the indicative timetable change, OCI will provide notice of such changes by means of a press release and will announce final dates in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and stock exchange requirements. The actual timetable may differ, including significantly, from the timetable set out above.

The timing of the Offer, including the commencement, duration and closing of the Post-Closing Acceptance Period, remains subject to determinations made by NNS in accordance with the terms of the Offer. Changes to Offer-related milestones may impact the timing of subsequent steps in the process.

Except for events directly related to the Offer, the occurrence and timing of the milestones described above remain subject to the remaining conditions and implementation steps applicable to the Combination, including implementation of the Combination by the long-stop date of 30 December 2026.

data.title: General Motors To Pay $220 Mln To Settle Driver Data Privacy Claims
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - General Motors (GM) will pay $220 million to settle allegations that it improperly sold drivers' behavior and location data to brokers, who then provided the information to insurers that could use it to set or increase insurance rates.

The settlement with 35 U.S. states and the District of Columbia centers on GM's Smart Driver program, which enrolled millions of drivers between 2016 and its discontinuation in 2024. Authorities alleged GM marketed the service as a tool to improve driving safety while sharing customer data without adequate permission.

Under the settlement, GM must limit the driving information it collects and obtain express consent before collecting or sharing certain data. A third party will also assess the automaker's compliance with its new privacy program.

The agreement follows a $12.75 million California settlement in May and a separate deal with the Federal Trade Commission restricting GM from sharing vehicle geolocation and driver behavior data with consumer reporting agencies for five years.

data.title: GFL investor relations exit unrelated to potential deal - CTFN
data.description:
The exit of a GFL Environmental investor relations executive is unrelated to the potential sale of the trash hauler.

Mario Cortellacci, vice president of investor relations at GFL, is stepping down, according to an internal memo CTFN reported earlier on Friday.

GFL shares were moving higher on Friday as some investors were speculating that his exit could be related to the sales process. The shares closed up 0.4% on Friday.

Cortellacci is leaving the company to take a role as chief of IR at a company going public, according to the report.

The executive departure comes after GFL on Wednesday said in its Q3 earnings release that the board's special committee has given interested parties a final deadline of Nov. 9 to disclose their updated proposals.

CTFN reported Thursday that a sovereign fund is now involved in the bidding for the waste management company. The new bidder entered the sale process a few weeks ago and is not affiliated with the two consortia bidding for GFL.

data.title: ACA marketplace premiums rising by 13% in 2027
data.description:
Key points:
  • Health insurance premiums on state marketplaces will increase by an average of 13% for silver tier plans, according to a new analysis.
  • Insurers had proposed an average 15% hike. 
  • In states that run their marketplaces, the silver benchmark premium will rise an average of 16%, while in states where it is federally operated, the increase is 11%, the health policy organization KFF found.
  • Last year, the overall hike was 26%
  • "In their rate filings, insurers point to a higher-than-usual increase in the underlying cost of care, which is not unique to the ACA Marketplaces; some employer plans have also seen steep cost increases," KFF says.
  • The organization added that ACA enrollment declined in 2026 as enhanced income tax credits expired. Those with incomes above 400% of the federal poverty level may face difficulty getting coverage in 2027 as they no longer qualify for premium tax credits and must pay the full cost, KFF noted.

data.title: INOVIO Announces FDA Accelerated Approval of VOCERYQ™, an Immunotherapy to Reduce the Frequency of Surgery in Adults with Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis (RRP)
data.description:
• INOVIO delivers a new nonsurgical treatment option with a broad indication for adults living with RRP, a rare and debilitating disease that often requires surgery
  • VOCERYQ™ is a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy that targets the root cause of RRP: HPV-6 and HPV-11
  • INOVIO expects to make VOCERYQ available to order and ship in approximately 60 days, with full commercial launch in the first quarter of 2027
  • VOCERYQ represents the first U.S. FDA approved DNA medicine, validating INOVIO's novel platform technology
  • INOVIO will host a conference call Monday, November 2, 2026 at 8:00 AM ET

PLYMOUTH MEETING, Pa., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- INOVIO (), a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing DNA medicines to help treat and protect people from HPV-related diseases, cancer, and infectious diseases, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted accelerated approval for VOCERYQ (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd), previously referred to as INO-3107, to reduce the frequency of surgery in adults with RRP. This indication is approved under the accelerated approval program based on demonstrated complete response defined as no requirement for surgical intervention in the 12 months after treatment in the efficacy population. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent on verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory study(ies).

"With the approval of VOCERYQ, we believe our DNA medicine platform has the potential to transform the treatment paradigm for RRP by offering a patient-centric treatment option. VOCERYQ is designed to deliver what we understand matters most to patients, which is the reduction of the surgical burden caused by RRP," said Dr. Jacqueline Shea, INOVIO's President and Chief Executive Officer. "INOVIO is grateful to the patients, study investigators, and the RRP Foundation, who helped make this achievement possible, and also to the FDA, who recognized the significant unmet need in this patient community. We would like to thank our dedicated INOVIO team and their ongoing commitment to patients. We look forward to delivering VOCERYQ to the RRP community and believe it has the potential to become a new standard of care for this devastating disease."

The approval is supported by data from INOVIO's RRP-001 study which evaluated VOCERYQ in 32 adult patients with RRP who had two or more surgeries in the year prior to treatment. During the VOCERYQ dosing window, no additional papilloma surgical excisions were required in the protocol. Of the 32 patients, 26 patients required 3 or more surgeries for papilloma excision in the 12 months prior to treatment and were included in the efficacy evaluation (median number of surgical excisions in the 12 months prior to the first dose in the efficacy population was 4.5 (range: 3 to 8)). Seven out of the 26 patients (27% [95% CI: 12; 48%]) demonstrated a complete response, defined as requiring no surgical excision of papillomas, after 12 months of follow up, which is not expected as part of the natural history of the disease when untreated. The complete clinical data for VOCERYQ were published in Nature Communications and in The Laryngoscope, the leading journal for the specialists who treat RRP.

"This new FDA-approved therapy brings us an important step closer to ensuring every RRP patient has access to a non-surgical treatment option that works for them. In reaching this milestone, we have shown that patient voices matter in the drug development process," said Kim McClellan, President of the RRP Foundation. "Patients have often had to endure repeated surgeries to control their RRP disease, but now thanks to the INOVIO team and the patients and investigators involved in the clinical development program for VOCERYQ, a new option is available that has the potential to further transform the treatment landscape for RRP patients. We look forward to continuing to work with clinicians, regulators and our partners in the healthcare industry to further improve the quality of life for those living with RRP."

Dr. Simon Best, Associate Professor of Otolaryngology at Johns Hopkins University and a lead investigator for INOVIO's RRP-001 study, said, "The approval of VOCERYQ is an important step in improving the quality of life for RRP patients as every surgery carries the risk of laryngeal injury. I believe it is in the best interest of RRP patients that the standard of care quickly transition away from surgical interventions to immunotherapy after RRP is diagnosed."

VOCERYQ was found to be well tolerated, with the most common adverse reactions (incidence >5%) including injection site reactions, headache, fatigue, hypertension, nausea and dizziness. Most treatment-related adverse reactions were grade 1 and 2 and transient. There were no grade 4 or 5 common adverse events. All 32 patients completed the study. See additional Important Safety Information below.

To verify the clinical benefit of VOCERYQ, a confirmatory study is expected to be conducted. The FDA requires INOVIO to submit a draft protocol for the study by the end of 2026 with the expectation of aligning on a final protocol by mid-2027.

VOCERYQ was approved in combination with CELLECTRA® 5PSP, INOVIO's proprietary DNA medicine delivery device. INOVIO expects to make VOCERYQ available to order and ship in approximately 60 days and anticipates full field deployment during the first quarter of 2027. INOVIO has engaged Syneos Health to support the recruitment and deployment of our medical and commercial field teams.

Conference Call

INOVIO will host a conference call on Monday, November 2 at 8:00 AM ET to provide additional details regarding the approval, including key aspects of the label and commercialization. You can watch the webcast at https://app.webinar.net/6LNlx7kxyqd. Event details can be found on INOVIO's website in the Events & Presentations section at https://ir.inovio.com/events-and-presentations/default.aspx.

Conference Call Dial-In Number

Local/International (toll): 1-646-357-8785

North American Toll Free: 1-800-836-8184

About RRP

RRP is a rare, debilitating disease caused primarily by HPV-6 and/or HPV-11. RRP is characterized by the development of small, wart-like growths, or papillomas, in the respiratory tract. While papillomas are generally benign, they can cause severe, life-threatening airway obstruction and respiratory complications. RRP can also significantly affect quality of life for patients by affecting the voice box, limiting the ability to speak effectively. Surgery to remove papillomas is the current standard of care for RRP; however, the papillomas often grow back. INOVIO's market research to date with patients and healthcare professionals indicates that a reduction of even one surgery matters, because every surgery poses a significant risk of causing permanent damage to the vocal cords and comes with potential costs to the patient, including adverse impacts to both quality of life and finances. Based on ongoing analysis of claims data, INOVIO believes there is a prevalent population of at least 25,000 patients with RRP in the United States, with additional patients diagnosed each year.

About VOCERYQ™

VOCERYQ™ is a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy designed to reduce the frequency of surgery for adults with RRP. VOCERYQ targets the root cause of RRP by generating an immune response using DNA plasmids that encode for HPV-6 and HPV-11 antigens. VOCERYQ is administered using the CELLECTRA® delivery device. Following a standard-of-care surgical debulking of visible papilloma prior to the initial administration of VOCERYQ, no additional surgical intervention is required as part of the 9-week dosing regimen.

The FDA previously granted VOCERYQ both Orphan Drug and Breakthrough Therapy designations, and the European Commission granted INO-3107 Orphan Drug designation.

Learn more at www.voceryq.com.

INDICATIONVOCERYQ is indicated to reduce the frequency of surgical papilloma excisions in adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis.

This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on reduction in the frequency of surgical papilloma excisions. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory study(ies).

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

Warnings & Precautions: Injection site reactions have occurred with VOCERYQ injection. Monitor patients for local site reactions for at least 30 minutes after treatment and manage accordingly.

Electroporation Related Adverse Reactions: Procedure-related effects including muscle contractions, transient bleeding, and vasovagal reactions may occur. Avoid use in patients with ipsilateral ICDs/pacemakers, metal implants or skin abnormalities at treatment site.

Adverse Reactions: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >5%) are injection site reactions, headache, fatigue, hypertension, nausea and dizziness.

Please go to www.voceryq.com for full Prescribing Information, including Patient Information.

About INOVIO's DNA Medicines Platform

INOVIO's DNA medicines platform has two innovative components: precisely designed DNA plasmids, delivered by INOVIO's proprietary medical device, CELLECTRA. INOVIO uses proprietary technology to design its DNA plasmids, which are small circular DNA molecules that enable the body's cells to produce specific proteins to target and fight disease. INOVIO's proprietary CELLECTRA delivery devices are designed to optimally deliver its DNA medicines to the body's cells without requiring chemical adjuvants or lipid nanoparticles and without the risk of the anti-vector response historically seen with viral vector platforms.

About INOVIO

INOVIO is a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing innovative DNA medicines to help treat and protect people from HPV-related diseases, cancer, and infectious diseases. INOVIO's technology optimizes the design and delivery of DNA medicines that enable the body to manufacture its own disease-fighting tools. For more information, visit www.inovio.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X (formerly known as Twitter).

data.title: SVRN Shares Fall on Nasdaq Delisting Determination
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Shares of SVRN, formerly OceanPal, fell after the Nasdaq determined that its securities are subject to delisting.

Shares of SVRN fell 8.3% to $27.03 in after-hours trading on Friday. The stock was down 5.3% at $29.47 through Friday's market-close.

The company said it received a letter from the Nasdaq's Listing Qualifications Department that said the company didn't meet the terms of exception it was previously granted when it failed to file its annual 2025 Form 20-F report.

A hearing request in a filing delinquency matter holds the suspension of a company's securities for 15 days from the date of the request. The company plans to request a hearing by Nov. 6.

Shares of SVRN are expected to continue to trade on the Nasdaq at least through the 15-day stay period.

data.title: Microsoft, BMW introduce voluntary exit offers: How paying employees to quit could help firms retain committed workers
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- As major companies such as Microsoft and BMW introduce voluntary exit programmes, new research suggests that offering employees financial incentives to leave could help businesses reshape their workforces while retaining employees who are more committed to their organisations.

The approach, commonly known as a pay-to-quit or voluntary exit scheme, allows eligible employees to accept financial compensation in exchange for leaving their jobs. Research indicates that such programmes could help employers identify workers who are more inclined to move on while encouraging those who choose to stay to demonstrate greater commitment and work effort.

A study published in the Journal of Management Accounting Research examined how employees' attachment to their organisations influences their decisions to accept financial incentives to quit.

The research was conducted by Leslie Berger and Lan Guo of Wilfrid Laurier University, Kelsey Matthews of the University of Waterloo, and Bradley Ruffle of McMaster University in Canada.

The researchers examined how employees' identification with an organisation affected their willingness to accept financial incentives to resign.

The findings indicated that employees with weaker organisational attachment were more likely to accept the offers, while those with a strong sense of belonging generally preferred to remain, irrespective of the financial incentive.

The payments appeared to have the greatest influence on employees whose attachment to their organisations fell between these two groups.

Interestingly, the researchers also found that employees who rejected the exit offers subsequently demonstrated greater work effort than before. This suggests that voluntary exit programmes could influence not only workforce composition but also the behaviour of employees who decide to stay.

A separate study published in the Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Economics in 2026 examined the responses of 1,000 participants in an online experiment.

Participants who rejected a small financial payment to quit completed 33% more tasks than those in a control group. However, researchers could not conclusively establish whether the higher productivity resulted from rejecting the payment or reflected participants' existing motivation. The findings therefore suggest a possible relationship rather than proof of a direct causal link.

Microsoft announced a voluntary exit programme on October 26 for eligible employees in participating teams across India, the US, the UK and Canada.

In a company blog post, Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said the initiative would provide financial assistance and career-planning resources to employees considering opportunities outside the company.

The programme covers employees at level 70 and below in participating teams. Eligibility will depend on business priorities, customer commitments and workforce requirements.

According to a PTI report, approximately 60,000 employees globally were eligible, including workers in India. Microsoft has around 23,000 employees in the country.

Eligible employees in India reportedly have until December 1 to make their decision. The package is understood to include one month's base salary for every completed year of service, health insurance and career-transition support.

Microsoft has described the initiative as a time-limited programme to help participating business units adapt their workforce to changing requirements.

German automaker BMW has also introduced a voluntary severance programme as part of its broader cost-reduction strategy.

However, the initiative encountered an IT disruption after a large number of employees attempted to access their personalised offers through the company's internal human resources portal.

According to German publications Handelsblatt and Automobilwoche, approximately 40,000 eligible employees attempted to view their individual offers.

A BMW spokesperson told Automobilwoche that the portal experienced high usage after employees received notifications about the programme.

BMW aims to eliminate around 8,000 positions in Germany by the end of 2027, excluding employees directly involved in production. The company also plans to reduce departments and associated management positions by 20% by mid-2027.

Voluntary exit programmes can help businesses reduce workforce costs and restructure operations without resorting to compulsory layoffs. However, their financial benefits depend on several factors, including severance expenses, replacement costs and the skills of departing employees.

Companies also face the risk of losing experienced workers whose contribution is difficult to replace.

The research suggests that financial incentives may help distinguish between employees who are already considering leaving and those who remain committed to their organisations. However, the effectiveness of these programmes will depend on how they are designed and implemented.

For Microsoft and BMW, the eventual impact will depend on employee participation, the number of departures and the ability of the companies to maintain productivity with a reshaped workforce.
